question_text:
Trains A and B are $10\text{ km}$ apart, and are approaching the same train station.
Train A is $8\text{ km}$ from the train station on the bearing $071^\circ$. Train B is on the bearing $296^\circ$ from the train station.

subparts.stem: Display this information on a diagram.

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct diagram showing North lines, bearing of $296^\circ$, angle $71^\circ$, and distances

subparts.solution: Diagram showing the positions of points $S$, $A$, and $B$ relative to the North line at $S$, with bearing of $B$ from $S$ being $296^\circ$, angle between North and $A$ being $71^\circ$, $SA = 8\text{ km}$, and $AB = 10\text{ km}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Bearings are measured clockwise from North ($0^\circ$ to $360^\circ$).
step_by_step: Draw North reference lines at vertices $S$, $B$, and $A$.
Draw bearing of $B$ from $S$ as $296^\circ$ clockwise from North.
Draw $A$ at bearing $71^\circ$ from $S$ with distance $8\text{ km}$, and connect $AB = 10\text{ km}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Measuring bearings counterclockwise or confusing the reference point 'from'.

subparts.stem: Find the bearing of train B from train A.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using the sine rule to find angle $\alpha \approx 34.4^\circ$

subparts.solution: $\text{N}_1\widehat{\text{S}}\text{B} = 360^\circ - 296^\circ = 64^\circ$ {angles at a point}. $\therefore \text{B}\widehat{\text{S}}\text{A} = 64^\circ + 71^\circ = 135^\circ$. By the sine rule: $\frac{\sin\alpha}{8} = \frac{\sin 135^\circ}{10} \implies \sin\alpha = \frac{8\sin 135^\circ}{10} \implies \alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8\sin 135^\circ}{10}\right) \approx 34.4^\circ$. Now $\theta = 180^\circ - 135^\circ - \alpha \approx 180^\circ - 135^\circ - 34.4^\circ \approx 10.6^\circ$ {angles in a triangle}. $\text{N}_2\widehat{\text{A}}\text{S} = 180^\circ - 71^\circ = 109^\circ$ {co-interior angles}. $\therefore \text{bearing of } B \text{ from } A \approx 360^\circ - 109^\circ + 10.6^\circ \approx 262^\circ$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use angle relations around points, co-interior angles between parallel North lines, and the sine rule to determine bearings.
step_by_step: Apply the sine rule to find angle $\alpha$ at vertex $B$: $\alpha \approx 34.4^\circ$.
Use co-interior angles to find angle from South to North at $A$: $180^\circ - 71^\circ = 109^\circ$.
Calculate the bearing from North at $A$: $360^\circ - 109^\circ + 10.6^\circ \approx 262^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrect co-interior angle calculation between the two parallel North lines.

subparts.stem: Train B is travelling at an average speed of $7\text{ m}\text{ s}^{-1}$. Find, to the nearest second, the time it will take for train B to reach the train station.

mark_breakdown.desc: Applying the cosine rule to calculate side $BS$
Final time in seconds or minutes and seconds

subparts.solution: By the cosine rule: $\text{BS}^2 = 10^2 + 8^2 - 2(10)(8)\cos\theta \implies \text{BS} = \sqrt{10^2 + 8^2 - 2(10)(8)\cos\theta} \implies \text{BS} \approx \sqrt{10^2 + 8^2 - 2(10)(8)\cos 10.6^\circ} \approx 2.59\text{ km} \approx 2590\text{ m}$. Now $\text{time} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \approx \frac{2590}{7} \approx 370\text{ seconds}$. It will take about $370\text{ seconds}$ or $6\text{ minutes } 10\text{ seconds}$ for train B to reach the train station.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Find the distance using the cosine rule, convert units to meters, and use $\text{time} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}$.
step_by_step: Use cosine rule with angle $\theta \approx 10.6^\circ$ and adjacent sides $10\text{ km}$ and $8\text{ km}$ to find $BS \approx 2.59\text{ km}$.
Convert kilometers to meters: $2.59\text{ km} = 2590\text{ m}$.
Divide by speed $7\text{ m/s}$ to get the time in seconds.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to convert kilometers to meters before dividing by speed in m/s.
